title: Pink Grapefruit Marmalade
summary: A glowing pink marmalade of grapefruit segments and fine peel slivers, set with the fruit’s own pectin and brightened with lemon.
equipment: 7 × 250 ml glass jars with new lids
preserving pan or large heavy pan
2 small plates, chilled in the freezer

steps.title: Shred the peel
steps.text: Pare the coloured zest from the grapefruit with the peeler, leaving the bitter white pith behind, and cut it into 3 mm slivers.

steps.title: Segment
steps.text: Cut the remaining pith off the fruit and slice out the segments over a bowl. Tie the membranes, the leftover pith and all the grapefruit and lemon pips in the muslin; this bag supplies the natural pectin, so no bought pectin is needed.

steps.title: Soften the peel
steps.text: Put the segments, slivers, muslin bag, lemon juice and water in the pan and simmer 25-30 minutes, until a sliver of peel squashes easily between your fingers. Peel will not soften any further once sugar goes in.

steps.title: Squeeze the bag
steps.text: Let the bag cool enough to handle, then squeeze it firmly over the pan to release the thick pectin-rich juice and discard it. Sterilise the jars in a 140 °C (120 °C fan) oven for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Boil
steps.text: Add the sugar, stir over a low heat until dissolved, then boil rapidly for 15-20 minutes to 104-105 °C. Confirm the set with a cold plate: the marmalade should wrinkle when pushed.

steps.title: Pot
steps.text: Skim, rest 10 minutes, then fill the hot jars to 5 mm from the top and seal. Allow to set at room temperature overnight.

tips: Grapefruit can interact with some medicines, including certain statins and blood-pressure drugs. If you take regular medication, check with a pharmacist before eating it.
Removing the white pith from the zest is the key to a marmalade that is pleasantly, not harshly, bitter.
A frequent mistake is adding sugar before the peel is soft; sugar firms the peel, so it stays chewy.
Grapefruit is lower in pectin than lemons, so do not skip the muslin bag.
storage: Unopened jars keep in the fridge for up to 3 months, or in a cool cupboard for up to 1 year if processed in a boiling-water bath for 10 minutes. Once opened, refrigerate and use within 1 month. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
